<!-- Academic websites tend to die of neglect. You build one in a burst of -->
<!-- enthusiasm, and two years later the "Publications" page is missing your -->
<!-- last five papers because updating it means editing HTML in six places. -->
<!-- This site is my attempt to make neglect impossible — by making the update -->
<!-- cost exactly one row in one spreadsheet. -->

<!-- ## The one-file rule -->

<!-- Everything you see here — the publications list, the teaching table, my -->
<!-- Ph.D. students, awards, workshops, even the little citation badges — comes -->
<!-- from a single Excel workbook, `cv_data.xlsx`. The same file also builds my -->
<!-- PDF CV (a separate Quarto project that renders to LaTeX). When I publish a -->
<!-- new paper, I add one row to the `publications` sheet, hit render, and both -->
<!-- the CV and the website update themselves. -->

<!-- The machinery is deliberately boring: -->

<!-- - **Quarto** renders `.qmd` pages to a static website. -->
<!-- - **R** reads the Excel file at render time. Every page contains almost no -->
<!--   code — just calls like `print_publications()` or `print_teaching()`. -->
<!-- - **`helpers.R`** holds all of those functions in one place. If I want to -->
<!--   change how a publication entry looks, I edit one function, once. -->

<!-- ```r -->
<!-- # research.qmd, in its entirety (almost) -->
<!-- print_scholar_stats() -->
<!-- print_publications() -->
<!-- print_projects() -->
<!-- print_presentations() -->
<!-- ``` -->

<!-- ## Live data, with a safety net -->

<!-- Two things on this site fetch fresh data at render time. -->

<!-- The **Data Corner** on the homepage pulls India's inflation and GDP growth -->
<!-- from the World Bank API and caches the result, so an offline render still -->
<!-- works. -->

<!-- The **citation badges** are trickier, because Google Scholar has no API -->
<!-- and actively blocks scripts. So the badges resolve through a chain: try -->
<!-- scraping my Scholar profile live; if Google objects (it usually does), -->
<!-- use the cached result of the last successful scrape; failing that, use -->
<!-- figures I keep in the spreadsheet; and as a final tier, query -->
<!-- [OpenAlex](https://openalex.org) — a genuinely open scholarly database -->
<!-- with a free API that never blocks anyone. Four tiers so that the page -->
<!-- never shows an embarrassing `NA`. -->

<!-- The lesson generalises: **any live data source on a personal website needs -->
<!-- a fallback**, because your site will outlive the goodwill of whatever it -->
<!-- scrapes. -->

<!-- ## The animated background -->

<!-- The homepage background is a single HTML canvas drawing four layers: a -->
<!-- drifting network whose nodes are economic variables (π, y, i, ε…), floating -->
<!-- equations from the models I work with, small impulse-response panels that -->
<!-- sketch themselves and fade away, and — my favourite — a slowly rotating -->
<!-- **3-D time-varying impulse response surface**, with horizon on one axis, -->
<!-- time on the other, and the response size as height and colour. If you have -->
<!-- ever estimated a TVP-VAR, you have stared at exactly that ridge. -->

<!-- It is ~400 lines of dependency-free JavaScript with a settings block at -->
<!-- the top, and it politely disables itself for visitors who prefer reduced -->
<!-- motion. -->

<!-- ## Hosting: free and automatic -->

<!-- The site lives in a GitHub repository and deploys to **GitHub Pages**. A -->
<!-- GitHub Action re-renders everything in the cloud on every push: it -->
<!-- installs R and the handful of packages, runs Quarto, and publishes the -->
<!-- result. My entire deployment process is: -->

<!-- ```bash -->
<!-- git add . -->
<!-- git commit -m "New paper" -->
<!-- git push -->
<!-- ``` -->

<!-- Two minutes later the site is live. No server, no subscription, no -->
<!-- maintenance. -->

<!-- ## Two hard-won warnings -->

<!-- **Don't keep a Quarto project inside a Google Drive folder.** Drive's sync -->
<!-- client locks the output directory mid-render and you get cryptic -->
<!-- `PermissionDenied` errors and ghost folders that refuse to be deleted. -->
<!-- I moved the project out; peace followed. -->

<!-- **Don't trust a scrape that "succeeds".** When Scholar serves its CAPTCHA -->
<!-- page, the HTTP request returns 200 and the HTML parses fine — it just -->
<!-- contains no data. My first version printed `NA` into the CV because the -->
<!-- error handler never fired. Validate the *content*, not the status code. -->

<!-- ## Was it worth it? -->

<!-- The honest cost was a few afternoons of setup. The payoff is that the -->
<!-- marginal cost of staying current is now one spreadsheet row. For an -->
<!-- academic website, that is the whole game: the best system is the one you -->
<!-- will actually keep feeding. -->

<!-- hosting) lives in the repository, and the source is a good starting point -->
<!-- if you want to build something similar.* -->
